It explicitly calls `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::add_dummy_assignment` when coverage instrumentation requires a dummy assignment, and calls `impl<'tcx> Scopes<'tcx>::scope_index` when translating lexical scopes into drop ranges.

Builds the deferred else-path exit for an `if`/`match`-style control-flow edge by finding the target lexical scope, collecting drops from inner scopes into the active `if_then_scope` drop tree, registering the current block as an entry, and installing a dummy terminator to be overwritten later. It explicitly calls `impl<'tcx> Scopes<'tcx>::scope_index`, `impl DropTree::add_drop`, and `impl DropTree::add_entry`.

Lowers all drops for the current top lexical scope on normal exit, first checking whether value drops require unwind cleanup and then building the scope’s drop sequence with the appropriate unwind/generator settings. It explicitly calls `impl Scope::needs_cleanup`.

Computes effective lint-root HIR IDs for the current and parent nodes, using maximal coverage mode to keep the original IDs or otherwise calling `maybe_lint_level_root_bounded` for bounded lint-root discovery. If the roots differ, it creates and installs a new source scope by calling `new_source_scope` with an explicit lint level for the current root.

Walks upward from a HIR node to find the nearest lint-root boundary within the current owner, stopping at the builder's root, at a node with lint attributes, or when a cached ancestor is encountered. It queries HIR metadata via `hir`, `attrs`, and `parent_id`, checks lint attributes with `Level::from_attr`, and records successful root-to-owner results in the cache with `contains`/`insert`.

Creates and returns a new MIR source scope inheriting parent lint-root and safety information unless explicit overrides are provided, and stores it in `self.source_scopes`. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Builds a `SourceInfo` value from the given span and the builder’s current source scope. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Returns the current lexical region scope for the builder. It explicitly calls `impl<'tcx> Scopes<'tcx>::topmost`.
Schedules both the storage cleanup and value drop for a local in the given region scope. It explicitly calls `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::schedule_drop` twice.

Schedules a deferred storage or value drop for a local in the appropriate lexical scope, skipping value drops for types that do not need dropping, validating storage drops for non-arguments, and invalidating cached cleanup paths in enclosing scopes before appending the new drop. It explicitly calls `impl Scope::invalidate_cache` on affected scopes.

Scans the given operands for `Operand::Move` values that are plain locals in the current top lexical scope, and records those locals in `scope.moved_locals` when that scope already has a `DropKind::Value` drop scheduled for them. It calls `Builder::local_scope` to verify it is operating on the topmost local scope.

Computes and caches the unwind drop-chain for the current scope stack by reusing the nearest `cached_unwind_block` and extending it with uncached scope drops. For each applicable drop it calls `DropTree::add_drop` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops`, including only `DropKind::Value` drops unless lowering a generator.

Builds or reuses the deferred unwind-drop chain needed when control diverges to a target scope. It first resolves the target scope index by calling `scope_index`, searches enclosing scopes for a cached unwind drop chain, and for uncached scopes extends that chain by calling `add_drop` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops` for each relevant drop before caching the resulting drop index on each scope.

Registers the unwind cleanup path for a block whose terminator may unwind. It calls `Builder::diverge_cleanup` to obtain the current unwind drop node, then calls `DropTree::add_entry` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops` to connect `start` into that cleanup tree.

Emits a `DropAndReplace` terminator with a fresh normal-successor block, then wires the source block into unwind cleanup. It calls `Builder::source_info`, creates the successor block, calls `Builder::diverge_from` to register the unwind path, and returns the successor as `BlockAnd<()>`.

Emits an `Assert` terminator with a fresh success block and arranges for unwinding cleanup from the asserting block. It calls `Builder::source_info`, creates the success block, calls `Builder::diverge_from` to connect the block to the unwind drop tree, and returns the success block.

Clears all scheduled drops from the current top scope after checking the region matches, and invalidates that scope's cached cleanup links. It calls `Scope::invalidate_cache` after emptying `top_scope.drops`.

Lowers one lexical scope's scheduled drops into MIR blocks in reverse order, building the normal-exit chain and connecting value-drop unwind edges to the shared unwind drop tree while skipping moved locals on non-unwind paths. When handling `DropKind::Value` entries it calls `DropTree::add_entry` on `unwind_drops` to associate the current block with the next unwind target.

Builds MIR for a normal control-flow exit drop tree and then links any value-dropping nodes in that tree to the shared unwind cleanup tree. It calls `DropTree::build_mir` to materialize the exit tree, calls `Builder::diverge_cleanup` to get the unwind root when needed, and calls `DropTree::add_drop` plus `DropTree::add_entry` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops` to construct and attach corresponding unwind drop paths.

Finalizes deferred drop trees at the end of MIR construction by choosing the generator-specific or normal unwind lowering path. It calls `Builder::build_generator_drop_trees` when `generator_kind` is present; otherwise it calls `Builder::build_unwind_tree` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops`.

Materializes an unwind drop tree into cleanup MIR blocks and ensures its root resumes unwinding if no shared resume block existed yet. It calls `DropTree::build_mir` to lower the tree and then emits a `Resume` terminator for the root block when initializing `resume_block`.
Creates a new ordinary MIR block for lowering an exit-scope drop node. It calls `CFG::start_new_block`.
Creates a new cleanup MIR block for lowering an unwind drop node. It calls `CFG::start_new_cleanup_block`.
Trait hook for connecting an existing MIR block to the entry block of a lowered drop-tree path. This is an abstract method and does not call other methods from the list.
Registers a `(drop node, source block)` pair as an entry into the drop tree after asserting the target drop index is valid. It does not call other methods from the list.

Builds cleanup for an explicit tail call by collecting movable argument locals, threading them into unwind paths, scheduling extra unwind entry points for scope drops, and emitting storage-dead cleanup blocks. It explicitly calls `impl DropTree::add_drop` and `impl DropTree::add_entry_point` on the unwind drop tree.

Extends the coroutine-suspend drop tree from the nearest cached scope, adds all uncached scope drops in order, caches the resulting drop-chain head per scope, and records the yield block as an entry point into that chain. It explicitly calls `impl DropTree::add_drop` and `impl DropTree::add_entry_point`.

Lowers the coroutine drop tree into MIR, installs the root `CoroutineDrop` terminator, builds the normal unwind tree, then adds unwind entry points for value-drop nodes in the coroutine drop tree and builds that unwind tree as well. It explicitly calls `DropTree::build_mir`.

Implements drop-tree entry linking for normal scope exits by replacing the placeholder `UnwindResume` terminator in the source block with a `Goto` to the drop-tree entry block. It does not call other methods from the list.
Creates a fresh MIR basic block for coroutine-drop tree lowering. It does not call other methods from the list.
Implements drop-tree entry linking for coroutine suspension by writing the drop-tree entry block into the `drop` field of a `Yield` terminator. It does not call other methods from the list.

Implements drop-tree entry linking for unwinding by attaching or rewriting unwind edges so they enter the supplied cleanup block, including creating a `Goto` in an existing cleanup block when needed. It does not call other methods from the list.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/build/expr/: Builds an operand whose temporary lifetime is limited to the current local scope. It calls `local_scope` to obtain that scope, then calls `as_operand` with `NeedsTemporary::Maybe` and no `LocalInfo`.
Builds a call argument operand scoped to the current local scope. It calls `local_scope` to compute the scope, then calls `as_call_operand` with that scope.

Lowers an expression into a MIR `Operand`, handling nested `ExprKind::Scope` by calling `source_info`, `in_scope`, and recursively `as_operand` on the scoped value. For non-scope expressions, it classifies the expression and either calls `as_constant` to emit a direct constant operand when allowed, or calls `as_temp` to materialize the value into a temporary, optionally recording `local_info`, and returns it as a move operand.

Lowers an expression into a call-argument operand, with special handling for unsized moved arguments. It handles nested `ExprKind::Scope` by calling `source_info`, `in_scope`, and recursively `as_call_operand`; when `unsized_fn_params` is enabled and the argument is an unsized `Deref`, it calls `as_temp` on the deref base and returns a moved dereferenced place; otherwise it falls back to `as_operand`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_borrowck/src/lib.rs::prov: Registers the `mir_borrowck` query provider in `Providers`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_borrowck/src/lib.rs::mir_: Top-level MIR borrowck query entry point: fetches promoted MIR, skips tainted/injected bodies by returning a default `BorrowCheckResult`, otherwise builds an inference context and calls `do_mir_borrowck` to run borrow checking.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_borrowck/src/lib.rs::do_m: Drives the full borrow-checking pipeline for one MIR body: creates a `BorrowckInferCtxt` via `BorrowckInferCtxt::new`, renumbers regions, gathers move data, runs initialization dataflow, computes regions, visits MIR for borrow checking, reports errors, and records mutability usage. It also uses `MoveVisitor::visit_operand` when validating promoted bodies for illegal moves.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_borrowck/src/lib.rs::impl: Maps an initialization-requiring action to its noun form for diagnostics; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Maps an initialization-requiring action to a specific past-tense verb phrase for diagnostics; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Maps an initialization-requiring action to a generalized past-tense verb phrase for diagnostics; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Handles MIR operands during move visiting by detecting `Operand::Move` and delegating move validation to `check_movable_place` on the borrowck context. Calls `check_movable_place`.
Constructs a new `BorrowckInferCtxt` by building an inference context with opaque type inference enabled for the given item and initializing the region-origin map to empty.
Allocates a fresh general region inference variable from the underlying inference context, and in debug builds records its source `RegionCtxt` in `reg_var_to_origin` for later tracing.
Allocates a fresh NLL region inference variable from the underlying inference context, and in debug builds records its source `RegionCtxt` in `reg_var_to_origin` for diagnostics/debugging.

Pre-registers concrete opaque types from HIR type checking for the next solver by re-instantiating their regions with fresh NLL variables and then injecting each hidden type. Calls `inject_new_hidden_type_unchecked`.
Implements `Deref` for `BorrowckInferCtxt` by returning the wrapped inference context.

Processes each MIR statement before its primary effect, first checking two-phase borrow activations and then dispatching borrow/use/mutation checks according to statement kind such as assignments, fake reads, intrinsics, and storage death. Calls `check_activations`, `consume_rvalue`, `mutate_place`, `check_if_path_or_subpath_is_moved`, `consume_operand`, and `access_place`.

Processes each MIR terminator before its primary effect, checking activations and then validating operand consumption, drops, calls, assertions, and destination mutations based on terminator kind. Calls `check_activations`, `consume_operand`, `access_place`, and `mutate_place`.

Performs post-terminator borrow checks, rejecting yields that keep local borrows alive in movable coroutines and validating that exiting control-flow invalidates no still-live borrow. Calls `check_for_local_borrow` and `check_for_invalidation_at_exit`.
Returns the MIR body currently being borrow-checked.

Central entry point for checking an access to a place: it suppresses duplicate or invalid activation reports, checks mutability/permission rules, checks borrow conflicts, and records that an error was reported for the place if either check fails. Calls `check_access_permissions` and `check_access_for_conflict`.

Checks whether a read/write/reservation/activation conflicts with any in-scope borrow, using Polonius output when enabled, and emits the appropriate borrow conflict diagnostics while suppressing compatible cases such as self-activation or allowed two-phase behavior. Calls `report_use_while_mutably_borrowed`, `buffer_error`, `report_conflicting_borrow`, `report_borrowed_value_does_not_live_long_enough`, `report_illegal_mutation_of_borrowed`, and `report_move_out_while_borrowed`.
Checks that a destination place is valid to assign through, then treats the assignment as a mutable write access. Calls `check_if_assigned_path_is_moved` and `access_place`.

Validates all place and operand uses inside an rvalue, translating borrows/addresses into the appropriate access kinds, checking moved/uninitialized state, recursively consuming nested operands, and propagating closure upvar mutability information for closure-like aggregates. Calls `access_place`, `check_if_path_or_subpath_is_moved`, `consume_operand`, and `propagate_closure_used_mut_upvar`.

Marks locals or captured upvars as mutably used when a closure/coroutine capture operand corresponds to a mutated place, handling direct upvar projections, deref-based mutation through mutable references, and nested closure capture propagation. Calls `is_upvar_field_projection`.

Checks the borrow semantics of an operand use: copies are read accesses plus moved-state checks, moves additionally validate movability and record a move write access, while constants need no action. Calls `access_place`, `check_if_path_or_subpath_is_moved`, and `check_movable_place`.

Checks whether a live borrow would be invalidated when the function exits, accounting specially for thread-local references, and reports a lifetime error if the borrowed place conflicts with the root place being dropped. Calls `report_borrowed_value_does_not_live_long_enough`.

Rejects borrows of local data that remain live across a coroutine yield by building and buffering the corresponding diagnostic. Calls `cannot_borrow_across_coroutine_yield`, `retrieve_borrow_spans`, and `buffer_error`.
Processes newly activated two-phase mutable borrows at a location by re-checking the borrowed place as an activation access. Calls `access_place`.
Determines whether a place may be moved from by walking its projections and recording move errors for borrowed content, fields of types with destructors, and other illegal move origins.

Checks whether the nearest tracked move path for a place is currently uninitialized/moved and, if so, reports an illegal use for the requested action. Calls `move_path_closest_to` and `report_use_of_moved_or_uninitialized`.

For array subslice uses, scans constant-index child move paths within the selected range and reports if any covered element or descendant is moved/uninitialized. Calls `move_path_for_place` and `report_use_of_moved_or_uninitialized`.

Checks whether a place, one of its tracked prefixes, or one of its shallow descendants is moved/uninitialized before the requested action, with special handling for array subslices. Calls `check_if_full_path_is_moved`, `check_if_subslice_element_is_moved`, `move_path_for_place`, and `report_use_of_moved_or_uninitialized`.
Finds the exact move path for a place or the nearest tracked parent move path and returns both the corresponding place prefix and move-path index.
Returns the exact move-path index for a place if borrowck tracks that place directly, or `None` when only a parent path exists.

Ensures an assignment target is valid to write through by walking projections and requiring the appropriate base or parent initialization for dereferences, destructor-bearing ADTs, tuple/field writes, and similar cases. Calls `check_if_full_path_is_moved`, `check_if_path_or_subpath_is_moved`, and the helper `check_parent_of_field`.

Helper for field assignments that searches shallow prefixes of the base place for the shortest moved/uninitialized ancestor and reports that specific move error, while permitting field reinitialization scenarios that should remain legal. Calls `move_path_for_place` and `report_use_of_moved_or_uninitialized`.

Enforces mutability and reassignment rules for a place access, distinguishing mutable borrows, mutations, reads, and special cases, recording used-mut information when allowed and otherwise reporting illegal reassignment or mutability errors. Calls `is_mutable`, `add_used_mut`, `is_local_ever_initialized`, `report_illegal_reassignment`, and `report_mutability_error`.
Returns an initialization index if the given local has ever been initialized according to the move/init tracking and current dataflow state.

Records that a local or captured upvar is meaningfully mutably used, based on whether the root place is a reassigned local or an upvar field projection. Calls `is_local_ever_initialized` and `is_upvar_field_projection`.

Determines whether a MIR place may be mutated and returns the mutable root place if so, otherwise the offending place. For projections, it recursively calls `is_mutable` on the base place, uses `is_upvar_field_projection` to adjust rules for captured upvars, and queries place types through `body`/`ty` to distinguish references, raw pointers, boxes, and other projection kinds before deciding mutability.
Checks whether a place is a closure upvar field projection by delegating to the path utility with the current MIR body. It calls `body` to supply the body context.
Returns the cached-on-demand dominator tree for the current MIR body’s basic blocks.
Returns the span used to sort buffered diagnostics, extracting it from either the `Error` or `NonError` variant.
Constructs an empty diagnostic buffer set for borrow checking, initializing move-error, mut-error, and general diagnostic storage.
Appends an error diagnostic to the buffered diagnostic list as a `BufferedDiag::Error`.
Appends a non-error diagnostic to the buffered diagnostic list as a `BufferedDiag::NonError`.
Forwards an error diagnostic into the shared borrow-check diagnostic buffer by calling `BorrowckDiags::buffer_error`.
Forwards a non-error diagnostic into the shared borrow-check diagnostic buffer by calling `BorrowckDiags::buffer_non_error`.
Deduplicates and stores a move error keyed by its move-out indices. If an older entry is replaced, it calls `cancel` on the old diagnostic and reports failure; otherwise it reports success.
Removes and returns the buffered mutable-borrow diagnostic for a span, if present, using swap-removal from the mut-error map.
Stores a mutable-borrow diagnostic and its repeat count under the given span.

Flushes all buffered borrow-check diagnostics and emits them in span order, returning the last emitted hard error if any. It merges deduplicated move and mutability errors into the main buffer, calls `sort_span` while sorting, may call `note` to summarize excess mutable-borrow errors, and finally calls `emit` on each buffered diagnostic.
Checks whether the general buffered diagnostic list is empty and returns that emptiness result.
Looks up whether a move error has already been buffered for the given move-out index sequence and returns the stored place/diagnostic pair if found.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/build/match: Lowers boolean and `let` conditions into MIR control flow with short-circuiting for `&&`, `||`, and `!`, including scope handling and branching to the enclosing `else`/break target on failure. It recursively calls `then_else_break` for nested logical operands, uses `lower_let_expr` for `let` conditions, and otherwise materializes the condition via `as_temp` before emitting an `if_` terminator or `break_for_else`/`goto` edges as needed.

Recursively lowers boolean/let conditions into MIR control flow, handling `&&`, `||`, `!`, and general condition expressions with proper scoping, branch coverage, and else-breaking behavior. It explicitly calls itself recursively via `then_else_break_inner` for nested logical operands, and also uses `visit_coverage_branch_operation`, `in_if_then_scope`, `local_scope`, `visit_unary_not`, `instrument_coverage`, `push_coverage_span_marker`, `source_info`, `break_for_else`, `in_scope`, `lower_let_expr`, `mcdc_increment_depth_if_enabled`, `as_temp`, `mcdc_decrement_depth_if_enabled`, `if_`, and `visit_coverage_branch_condition` to build the resulting CFG.

Top-level match lowering entry point that lowers the scrutinee, builds per-arm candidates, constructs the decision tree, and then lowers arm bodies. It calls `lower_scrutinee`, `create_match_candidates`, `lower_match_tree`, and `lower_match_arms`.

Lowers the match scrutinee into a `PlaceBuilder` and injects a `FakeRead` when the place can be resolved, ensuring safety/initialization checks even for uninhabited scrutinees. It calls `as_place_builder`.
Creates one `Candidate` per match arm pattern, recording whether the arm has a guard and cloning the shared scrutinee place for each candidate. It calls `Candidate::new`.

Lowers each match arm body inside its scope by declaring bindings, binding the selected candidate, and lowering the arm expression into the destination, then joins arm end blocks. It calls `declare_bindings`, `bind_pattern`, and `expr_into_dest`.

Converts a matched candidate (or its leaf subcandidates) into binding/guard code, avoiding extra blocks for a single candidate and handling drop scheduling across alternatives. It calls `bind_and_guard_matched_candidate` directly for leaf candidates, or `traverse_candidate` to walk subcandidates before calling `bind_and_guard_matched_candidate` for each leaf.

Lowers an initializer expression into an irrefutable pattern, using direct fast paths for simple by-value bindings and typed bindings, and otherwise lowering through place-based pattern matching. In the optimized cases it calls `storage_live_binding`, `expr_into_dest`, and `schedule_drop_for_binding`; in the general case it calls `as_place_builder` and `place_into_pattern`.

Matches an existing place against an irrefutable pattern, optionally records the matched place into user-variable metadata, and then performs the actual binding. It calls `Candidate::new`, `lower_match_tree`, and `bind_pattern`.

Declares all primary bindings introduced by a pattern, creating a visibility scope on demand and attaching guard/match-place metadata to each local; if the guard is an `if let`, it also declares bindings from the guard pattern. It calls `visit_primary_bindings`, `declare_binding`, and may recursively call `declare_bindings` for `Guard::IfLet`.

Recursively walks a guard expression to predeclare bindings introduced by `let` conditions and `&&`-chained guard structure. For `ExprKind::Let`, it calls `declare_bindings` to declare the pattern bindings; for `ExprKind::Scope` and `ExprKind::Use`, it calls `declare_guard_bindings` recursively on the wrapped expression; and for `ExprKind::LogicalOp { op: And, .. }`, it calls `declare_guard_bindings` recursively on both `lhs` and `rhs`. Other expression kinds are ignored.

Marks a binding local as `StorageLive`, optionally schedules its storage drop in the variable's region scope, and returns the corresponding `Place`. It calls `schedule_drop` when storage-drop scheduling is enabled and a variable scope exists.
Schedules a value drop for a binding local if that variable has an associated region scope. It calls `schedule_drop`.

Recursively walks a pattern and invokes the provided callback for each primary binding, threading projected user-type information through arrays, slices, dereferences, enum variants, and user type ascriptions. It recursively calls `visit_primary_bindings` on subpatterns.
Returns whether this pattern-extra-data carries no recorded bindings and no ascriptions by checking both underlying collections for emptiness.

Constructs a flattened pattern representation by first building an initial match-pair tree with `MatchPairTree::for_pattern`, recording whether the pattern is never via `is_never_pattern`, and then simplifying/refining the collected match pairs through `simplify_match_pairs`.
Constructs a fresh match candidate from a place and pattern, initializing its first match pair and empty binding/ascription/subcandidate state. It calls `MatchPair::new`.
Builds a fresh match candidate from a flattened pattern, transferring its match pairs and extra data and initializing all candidate bookkeeping fields to their empty state.
Checks whether the candidate’s first remaining match pair is an or-pattern test.
Visits every leaf candidate in a candidate tree by delegating to the generic candidate traversal helper. It calls `traverse_candidate`.

Generic recursive DFS helper over candidate trees that invokes a leaf callback for leaf candidates, otherwise recurses through children and then runs a completion callback. It recursively calls `traverse_candidate`.
Returns the underlying pattern range when this test case is the `Range` variant, or `None` otherwise.
Returns the underlying constant when this branch is the `Constant` variant, or `None` otherwise.

Builds the match decision tree, tracks optional fake borrows for guarded matches, links leaf candidates in priority order, and returns the fake-borrow temporaries to keep alive across guards. It calls `match_candidates`, `Candidate::visit_leaves`, and `calculate_fake_borrows`.

Simplifies candidate match pairs, flattens split or-pattern candidates when needed, and dispatches the simplified set to the main matching routine. It calls `simplify_candidate`, `Candidate::visit_leaves`, and `match_simplified_candidates`.

Processes the current candidate slice one step in the match-decision tree: it handles the empty case, selects an already matched leading candidate, expands or-pattern prefixes when needed, or performs another test, then continues with the remainder. It explicitly calls `select_matched_candidate`, `starts_with_or_pattern`, `expand_and_match_or_candidates`, `test_candidates`, and `match_candidates`.
Marks a fully satisfied leaf candidate as selected by recording its pre-binding block and allocating a fresh otherwise block for subsequent candidates. It explicitly calls `start_new_block`.

Expands the maximal safe prefix of candidates that can participate in one round of or-pattern expansion, lowers the expanded subcandidates, simplifies the result, and returns any remaining unexpanded candidates. It explicitly calls `starts_with_or_pattern`, `create_or_subcandidates`, `match_candidates`, `merge_trivial_subcandidates`, `remove_never_subcandidates`, and `test_remaining_match_pairs_after_or`.
Expands a candidate whose leading match pair is an or-pattern into one subcandidate per alternative pattern. It explicitly calls `Candidate::from_flat_pat` to build each generated subcandidate.
Recursively compresses guard-free subcandidate trees whose leaves carry no extra bindings or ascriptions into a single shared pre-binding block. It recursively calls `merge_trivial_subcandidates`.

Prunes subcandidates marked as never-patterns, emitting `Unreachable` terminators for their leaf pre-binding blocks, and if pruning empties the subtree, creates a replacement pre-binding block for the parent candidate. It explicitly calls `is_empty` only on collections, and among the summarized methods it directly calls the candidate leaf visitor (`visit_leaves`, not `visit_leaves_rev`), so it does not directly call another listed summarized method.

After an initial or-pattern expansion, propagates the remaining deferred or-pattern match pairs to each leaf subcandidate, recursively lowers them, and reconnects failure edges so repeated alternatives can be skipped when sound. It explicitly calls `match_candidates` and uses leaf traversal to update each leaf candidate.
Chooses the next test from the first candidate’s highest-priority remaining match pair and returns both the place to inspect and the derived test. It explicitly calls `pick_test_for_match_pair`.

Partitions the leading run of candidates according to the outcome branches of a chosen test, stopping once the test no longer applies to the next candidate, and returns both the untouched suffix and the grouped tested candidates. It explicitly calls `sort_candidate`.

Chooses a test from the highest-priority remaining match pair, enriches switch tests with additional cases from later candidates, partitions candidates by test outcome, performs the MIR branch, and recursively continues matching on each reachable branch. It calls `test`, `add_cases_to_switch`, `add_variants_to_switch`, `sort_candidate`, `perform_test`, and `match_candidates`.

Lowers a `let` condition by matching the expression against the pattern, branching to the `else` scope on failure, optionally declaring bindings, and binding the successful candidate on the success path. It calls `lower_scrutinee`, `Candidate::new`, `lower_match_tree`, `declare_bindings`, and `bind_pattern`.

Finalizes a fully matched candidate by setting up false edges for later candidates, applying type ascriptions, creating guard bindings and fake borrows, lowering any guard expression, and then binding variables for the arm body or let-success path. It calls `ascribe_types`, `bind_matched_candidate_for_guard`, `then_else_break`, `lower_let_expr`, and `bind_matched_candidate_for_arm_body`.
Emits MIR `AscribeUserType` statements for each stored pattern ascription on the given block. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Creates guard-time bindings for a matched candidate, always exposing identifiers in guards through shared references and preserving explicit by-ref bindings by creating both arm-time and guard-time locals. It calls `storage_live_binding`.

Creates arm-body bindings for a matched candidate, reusing already-live storages when requested, scheduling value drops, and assigning either moved/copied values or references according to the binding mode. It calls `storage_live_binding` and `schedule_drop_for_binding`.

Allocates and registers the MIR locals and debug info for one pattern binding, including the extra guard-reference local when the arm has a guard, and records the variable-to-local mapping. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/build/expr/: Stack-safe entry point for lowering an expression into a fresh MIR temporary. It wraps the real lowering in `ensure_sufficient_stack` and directly calls `as_temp_inner` to perform the actual work.

Core implementation that creates and configures a temporary `Local`, handles scoped expressions and special local metadata, emits storage/lifetime management, and lowers the expression into the temp. If the expression is `ExprKind::Scope`, it calls `source_info`, `in_scope`, and then recursively re-enters through `as_temp` on the scoped value. Otherwise it may call `currently_in_block_tail` and `block_tail` when annotating block-tail temporaries, uses `immutable` while finalizing `LocalDecl`, converts the temp with `from`, emits storage/drop handling including `schedule_drop`, and finally lowers the value by calling `expr_into_dest`.
